overview: For home health agencies, hospice agencies, hospitals, nursing homes and personal care homes ready to earn a greater share of referrals. Find the right sources with 150+ public healthcare datasets, focus your outreach, and turn consistent follow-up into stronger relationships. Bring market research, daily activity, and referral tracking together in one healthcare CRM.
legend: Features without a label are available to every role on every plan, within the plan’s territory and service-line allowance. Labels name additional role or plan requirements. The 30-day trial includes Pro features in one county, with your choice of healthcare service lines.

pillars.title: Understand the market
pillars.why: Analyze your market before committing time and budget. Compare counties and ZIP areas by demographics, growth since 2020, Medicare use, Medicare Advantage share and provider supply, and research the hospitals, practices, facilities and ownership groups around the areas you serve.

pillars.title: Build a more focused referral list
pillars.why: Research physicians and facilities by location, specialty, and service focus. Review profiles, practice locations, affiliations, and available public-data signals to build a list with a clear reason behind each target.

pillars.title: Keep every relationship moving
pillars.why: Keep every account in a CRM built for healthcare marketing: stages from target to preferred source, contacts by role from discharge planner to director of nursing, notes, visits, and follow-ups. Assign ownership, keep a shared history, and see which accounts need the team’s attention.

pillars.title: Give every visit a purpose
pillars.why: Prepare account briefs and call sheets, plan calls, visits, and routes, and log each visit from a phone. Log expenses against the account they were for, attach the receipt, and turn check-ins into mileage, so less routine work has to be reconstructed later.

pillars.title: Connect effort to outcomes
pillars.why: Keep track of recorded referrals, admissions, conversion, and lost reasons alongside visits and outreach. Review source, team, and location activity to decide where follow-up or a different approach is needed.

pillars.title: Bring clearer answers to the meeting
pillars.why: Use market, account, and decision briefs, prepared reports, and Ask the book’s supported questions to prepare for decisions. Import referral and admission facts from CSV reports to bring your organization’s results into the same workspace.

pillars.title: Spend with compliance in view
pillars.why: Value shared meals per person, follow each physician’s running total against the Stark annual limit, and flag meal caps, frequency, missing receipts, and duplicates. Managers approve, record reimbursement, and export register, compliance, and payroll reports.

pillars.title: Know the competition
pillars.why: Research competing providers, facilities, ownership, and available quality measures in your territory. Specialized Medicare share rankings and change alerts cover home health and hospice where the source data is available.

pillars.title: Reach contacts at scale
pillars.why: Send email campaigns to a lead list or the contacts on your book, with your sender details and automatic unsubscribe handling. Track deliveries, opens, clicks, and bounces.

pillars.title: Walk into every visit prepared
pillars.why: A pre-visit card shows the last visit and notes, referrals for the last 90 days against the 90 before, open tasks and up to four talking points. On Growth and Pro, say what happened afterwards and the AI proposes the visit note and next step for you to check.

pillars.title: Answer referrals faster
pillars.why: Each referral keeps when it came in, when it was first answered and when it was decided. See median hours to answer, the share answered within an hour and the slowest sources, and confirm the openings, counties and payers your organization can take.

pillars.title: Find where to grow next
pillars.why: Rank counties or ZIP areas for a new office by demand, growth, need and supply gap. Find hospitals and physicians with large public volume and few referrals logged, and read ready-made briefs on expansion, acquisition and referral development.
pillars.area: Site finder, referral discovery & market briefs

areas.name: Healthcare marketing CRM
areas.intro: The marketing book: the accounts you keep month to month, the people you know there, and everything your team has logged on them.

features.name: Marketing book of accounts
features.does: Keep hospitals, nursing homes, personal care and assisted living homes, physician practices, agencies and other referral sources in one book. Each account holds its type, city, phone, website, NPI, CCN, tags and owner.

features.name: Lines of business
features.does: Organize relationships by healthcare service line, including practices, hospitals, behavioral health, rehabilitation, diagnostics, senior care, home health, hospice, DME, and other healthcare services. One account can have a separate stage and history on each line.

features.name: Relationship stages
features.does: Move accounts through Target, Relationship, Active source, Preferred, At risk and Lost. The date of the last change is kept, and At risk or Lost asks why: competitor, service issue, staff turnover, moved or other.

features.name: Contacts by healthcare role
features.does: Record the administrator, director of nursing, business office, social services, admissions, discharge planner, case manager, physician liaison, physician, intake, MDS coordinator and executive director. Mark someone as left to keep their history and stop email to them.

features.name: Account page and full history
features.does: Notes, the next visit or call, referrals, expenses and campaigns on one page. Search the account’s whole activity history by note, employee or date. Print a one-page account sheet without notes.

features.name: Market position on every account
features.does: An account with a CCN or NPI shows its lead score, county and state share and rank, Medicare beneficiaries, star ratings, staffing, cost-report figures and discharge mix beside your own relationship history.

features.name: Month end view
features.does: Sales calls, referrals, admissions, calls per referral and a six-month trend. See which accounts are referring more or less, which you called with no referral, and which belong on next month’s schedule.

features.name: Search, filters and saved views
features.does: Search by name, city, tag, NPI or CCN. Filter by type, stage and data-quality flags, save a view as your default, share it by link, and change the stage of many accounts at once.

features.name: Spreadsheet import and export
features.does: Import up to 2,000 accounts and contacts from a CSV with column mapping and a preview, from a template if you want one. Matches fill blanks instead of creating copies. Export the book or the rows you tick.

features.name: Book hygiene
features.does: Possible duplicates are listed for a one-step merge. Chips flag accounts with no phone, no contact, no email, an invalid email or no call in 90 days, and engagement reads Healthy, Warm, Cold or No activity.

features.name: Going quiet
features.does: Accounts whose referrals dropped, or that have gone 45 days without a visit, are listed with the reason and marked on the book and in the Monday digest.

features.name: Compare accounts side by side
features.does: Compare two to four accounts on stage, contacts, visits, referrals and admissions, star ratings, Medicare share and recent activity. Save the comparison, print it or download a PDF.

features.name: Claim, release and hand off
features.does: Claim accounts for your own book. When someone leaves or changes territory, move their whole book to a teammate in one step. Visits and referrals already logged stay credited to the person who logged them.

features.name: Parent organizations
features.does: Group locations that belong to the same organization, from a shared parent name, practice name or people, or name the parent yourself.

features.name: Physician group certifications
features.does: Open a physician group in the market list to see which members certify home health or oversee hospice care, the patients Medicare published for each, who is on your book, what your book admitted from them in 12 months and an estimated share. Members CMS doesn’t list show as not listed, never zero, and high-volume members not on your book go to a lead list in one step.

features.name: Account tiers and visit cadence
features.does: Mark accounts tier A, B or C, or let Intel suggest tiers from each account's referrals. The organization sets how often each tier should be visited; Today and Team review show who is behind, the suggested route moves them up, and Monday's email lists them.

features.name: Call or text from an account
features.does: Call and Text open the phone's dialer or messages app from the account or a person there, then log the call (or a note for a text) in one tap. Nothing is placed or sent from Intel.

areas.name: Daily field work
areas.intro: The day on the road: what to do today, where to go, and a fast way to record each visit from a phone.

features.name: Today
features.does: Your workspace when you sign in: tasks with due dates and priorities (overdue ones stay marked), progress on this month’s goals, and up to ten accounts to visit this week, each with one reason.

features.name: Tasks and assignments
features.does: Create tasks for yourself, linked to an account or not. A manager can assign a task to a named teammate.

features.name: Schedule and call plan
features.does: Plan visits and calls by day on a weekly agenda. Reschedule or remove a pending activity, or complete it with an outcome so the plan note is kept and the visit is not logged twice.

features.name: Suggested route
features.does: Builds a day from follow-ups that are due, sources whose referrals fell, and key accounts with no visit in 45 days, then orders the stops as a route on a map. Order this week’s scheduled visits by drive time too.

features.name: Visit log built for a phone
features.does: Check in with the phone’s location, type or dictate the note, and start from an in-service, lunch or discharge-planner drop-in template. A next step with a date schedules the follow-up. A draft survives a refresh and a save can be retried without duplicates.

features.name: Pre-visit card
features.does: Before you walk in: the last visit and notes, referrals for 90 days against the 90 before, the oldest open referral, open tasks, the people on the account and what you left last time, with up to four talking points chosen from those figures. On a plan with AI briefs, an AI summary of your last notes.

features.name: Spoken visit debrief
features.does: Say or type what happened after a visit and the AI proposes the visit note, the next step and its date. Nothing is saved until you check the form and save the visit. Possible patient details are taken out before the AI reads anything. Each debrief, notes summary or paid voice note uses one of your organization’s daily AI requests (500 a day on Growth, 2,000 on Pro), and the Visit log shows how many are left.

features.name: Business card scan
features.does: Photograph a business card on an account and the phone reads the name, role, phone and email for you to check before the contact is saved. On Growth and Pro a paid reader takes over when the phone finds no name, using one AI request.

features.name: County call sheets
features.does: A working list for a county: hospitals, home health agencies, hospices, nursing homes, clinicians, DME suppliers, licensed homes and dialysis facilities. Mark each Call, Visit or Account and it lands on the marketing book. Print the schedule or the chart of accounts.

features.name: Follow-up emails
features.does: Send one email to a contact and book a dated visit in one step. Members schedule the visit and an owner sends the email; every email carries an unsubscribe link and your postal address.

features.name: Calendar sync
features.does: Download your scheduled visits and calls, subscribe with a private calendar link, or sync them to Outlook or Google Calendar. Notes are never copied to the calendar.
features.access: Outlook and Google sync: where configured

features.name: Weekly book digest
features.does: A Monday email for each marketer: last week’s visits, the coming week’s follow-ups, referral changes on their accounts, accounts going quiet, overdue tasks, new or moved physicians and sources falling off pace.

features.name: On your phone’s home screen
features.does: Add CareMetric Intel to a phone’s home screen and it opens like an app.

features.name: Hands-free on the road
features.does: Have the phone read the pre-visit card aloud (never your notes), ask the AI Assistant by voice where it is open, and open directions to the account in Google Maps, Apple Maps or Waze.

areas.name: Expenses, mileage and reimbursement
areas.intro: Expense reports built for healthcare marketing: spend is logged against the referral source it was for, valued per person, checked against the Stark limit and your policy, approved, and paid.

features.name: Expenses logged by account
features.does: Record the account, date, amount, business purpose and payment method (corporate card, personal card, out-of-pocket cash, company check). Categories cover meals, gifts, entertainment, education and in-services, promotional items, mileage, per diem and events. Cash and gift cards are deliberately not offered.

features.name: Receipt capture
features.does: Take a photo or upload an image or PDF and it attaches when you save. Where receipt reading is configured, the amount, date, vendor and a suggested category and account are read from it for you to check.

features.name: Per-person value for shared meals
features.does: List everyone who partook and the expense is split among them, the valuation rule CMS sets for shared benefits (42 CFR 403.904(g)(1)). Each person’s value builds up across the year.

features.name: Stark annual limit tracking
features.does: Each physician’s running total is measured against the Stark nonmonetary-compensation limit for the year (42 CFR 411.357(k)), with a warning as it gets close. The limit itself blocks approval unless a manager overrides it with a logged comment.

features.name: Non-physician policy totals
features.does: Spend on discharge planners, case managers and other referral sources builds up against an internal policy alert you set. It is an alert, not a legal safe harbor: the Anti-Kickback Statute names no dollar threshold.

features.name: Policy checks and flags
features.does: Per-meal caps by meal (breakfast, in-service lunch, out-of-office lunch, dinner), a per-diem cap, meals per person per month and per 12 months, large single benefits, entertainment, missing receipts, documentation gaps and possible duplicates are all flagged.

features.name: Approval workflow
features.does: Save a draft, then submit. Clean, fully documented expenses under your approval threshold approve themselves; flagged ones wait in a manager’s queue to be approved or denied with a note. A denied expense can be corrected and resubmitted.

features.name: Reimbursement tracking
features.does: Approved and paid are separate facts. A manager records the paid date, method (payroll, direct deposit, check) and batch, one expense or a whole batch at a time. Marketers cannot mark their own expenses reimbursed.

features.name: Budgets and compliance settings
features.does: Set a monthly budget per marketer, the approval and receipt-required thresholds, meal and per-diem caps, frequency limits, the warning percentage, the mileage rate and the non-physician policy total.

features.name: Who you’ve spent on
features.does: Every marketer sees each person they have spent on this year, their running value against the limit, and their meal counts. The same totals appear on each account’s page.

features.name: Expense reports and exports
features.does: An itemized register, totals by marketer and by account, a compliance report and a payroll / AP export, for any date range, marketer, category or status. Download CSV or PDF.

features.name: Scheduled expense reports
features.does: Email any expense report daily, weekly or monthly to the managers you choose. Send a test, pause or edit a schedule at any time.

features.name: Mileage log
features.does: Adds the straight-line miles between each day’s visit check-ins and prices them at your organization’s mileage rate. Turn a day into a mileage expense draft in one step, then submit it like any other expense. Download the log as CSV.

areas.name: Referral and admission tracking
areas.intro: Your organization’s own results: the referrals each source sends, what became of them, and which relationships are slipping.

features.name: Log referrals and outcomes
features.does: Record a referral on the account it came from, with the service, payer and a note. Mark it admitted or not admitted, with the reason, when you know.

features.name: Response time
features.does: Each referral keeps the time it came in, when it was first answered and when it was decided. Results reports median hours to first answer and to decision, the share answered within an hour, after-hours arrivals and the slowest sources.

features.name: EMR report imports
features.does: Import referrals and admissions from CSV reports with column mapping and a preview. Saved layouts cover common home health and hospice EMR reports. Upload a file, pick one up from an SFTP drop folder, or forward it to an email-in address. Patient-identifying columns are dropped and never stored.

features.name: Scheduled EMR report delivery
features.does: Some EMR reports can be delivered on a schedule your organization controls, with a delivery health page that shows the interval, observed dates and source totals. A file with rejected rows is held instead of imported.

features.name: Referral funnel
features.does: Referrals received, admitted and not admitted, and why, by account and by marketer.

features.name: Referral drop-off alerts
features.does: Flags a top source when its last 30 days fall at least 30% below its average month from the 90 days before. An owner can set the drop anywhere from 10% to 90%.

features.name: Outcomes packet
features.does: A one-page quarterly PDF for a hospital or facility: the referrals they sent, how many were admitted and how fast they were answered, your organization’s public star rating, readmissions and quality scores, and the availability you confirmed. Hospitals in CMS’s TEAM model are flagged, with a list of TEAM hospitals to target. No patient names, notes or clinical detail.

features.name: Lost reasons
features.does: Totals the reasons behind every lost and at-risk account, shows how many have no reason recorded, and lists the accounts.

features.name: Admissions forecast
features.does: Estimates how many open referrals will be admitted, from your last 180 days, as a range that stays wide when the history is short.

features.name: Availability
features.does: A dated confirmation of what your organization can take: accepting, limited or closed to new referrals, confirmed openings, earliest start, counties, disciplines, payers, languages and weekend coverage. Expired confirmations read as unconfirmed.

features.name: Why a source is slipping
features.does: For a source on the drop-off list, see what the book shows over the same months: a contact who left, referrals not admitted, availability you gave, fewer visits, a service ticket, slower responses, a physician who moved and a watched competitor nearby. Add the next step as a task in one tap.

features.name: Shareable profile link
features.does: A revocable page for referral sources, by location: intake phone and fax, services, current confirmed availability, public CMS ratings and the median first response to referrals, with a QR code and a view count. No patient information.

areas.name: Prospecting and targeting
areas.intro: Find the physicians, practices and facilities worth a relationship, with a reason behind each name on the list.

features.name: Provider and facility directory
features.does: Search providers, organizations, practice locations and facilities by name, NPI, specialty and place. Profiles show locations, taxonomies, affiliations and available Medicare activity.

features.name: Target Builder
features.does: Filter providers by state, city, ZIP, specialty, score range, Medicare patient volume, Medicare participation and behavioral-health or geriatric focus, then save the matches as a list.

features.name: Saved lead lists
features.does: Work a list with a status for each provider (New, Contacted, Qualified, Not a fit), add to it from any provider page or search, and export it.

features.name: Referral-source rankings
features.does: Rank a county’s clinicians by a referral index built on public Medicare data, including the patients they certified for home health, and add the top names to a list in one step.

features.name: New physicians
features.does: Physicians newly listed in your area in the last 45 days, and people already on your book whose practice address or facility changed.

features.name: Referral discovery
features.does: Compare public volume with the referrals you have logged to find under-worked hospitals and physicians, see hospice planning estimates, and spot counties with high need and little local supply.

features.name: Physician share
features.does: Your admissions from each physician divided by the home health certifications or hospice care-plan oversight Medicare published for them, banded as mostly yours, split, rarely yours or none yet. A labeled estimate from public counts.

features.name: Opportunity scores
features.does: Providers in the scored states carry a lead score from CareMetric’s scoring rules, and the provider’s page shows what went into it. A provider without one reads Unscored; a score is never invented.

areas.name: Market and territory research
areas.intro: The people, providers and Medicare activity in the places you serve, within your plan’s territory.

features.name: Territory map
features.does: Providers on a map of a state in your territory, highest lead scores first. Filter by specialty group, entity type, score range and patient volume, color by score, or switch on a heat map. A county-density tab ranks counties by practice locations.

features.name: County intelligence
features.does: A county’s older-adult population, income and adults living alone; the hospitals its residents use and where their post-discharge spending goes; current Medicare facility listings with published-county or labeled ZIP-based membership; historical post-acute providers assigned by their reported ZIP; and top referral sources.

features.name: Demographics by county and ZIP area
features.does: Residents 65+, 75+ and 85+, median age, household income and home value, poverty, uninsured, disability, Medicare-Medicaid dual coverage and 65+ households living alone, for a county and each of its ZIP areas, with the change in residents since 2020.

features.name: Community and payer context
features.does: On each county: Medicare Advantage plans, penetration, star ratings and supplemental benefits, Medicaid managed care where CMS publishes it, chronic disease prevalence, social vulnerability, shortage areas, healthcare wages, Part D prescribing and the most common Medicare services.

features.name: Site finder
features.does: Rank a state’s counties, or the ZIP areas of a state or county, for a new office or facility. Pick a service line and compare demand, growth since 2020, need and the supply gap; the opportunity index averages each area’s percentile among the areas compared. Download it as CSV.

features.name: Market data and market share
features.does: Each county’s Medicare enrollment and Medicare Advantage share, home health, hospice and skilled nursing use and supply, spending and readmissions, and agency shares using the displayed service-area or provider-ZIP method. Historical post-acute county assignments use the provider ZIP from the utilization year and the Census county containing most of that ZIP area; they can differ from current directory office counties.

features.name: Facility directory
features.does: Hospitals, home health agencies, hospices, nursing homes, inpatient rehab, long-term care hospitals, DME suppliers, community health centers, dialysis facilities, and state-licensed personal care and assisted living homes where loaded. Export DME suppliers to CSV or Excel from the DME report.

features.name: Facility profiles
features.does: Ownership, cost-report revenue and expenses, beds and visits, star ratings and quality measures, service areas and rank in the county and state. Print a branded profile.

features.name: Public quality scores
features.does: A hospice's Hospice Care Index and its Service and Spending Variation Index from CMS's FY2027 hospice rule, a home health agency's value-based purchasing score and payment adjustment, and whether a hospital is in CMS's TEAM model, on each facility page.

features.name: Utilization and CMS data
features.does: Medicare payments and service volume by specialty, and any clinician’s Medicare service lines by NPI.

features.name: Market briefs
features.does: Ready-made briefs for expansion (where to grow), acquisition (the largest operators in a state), hospital relationships and referral development.

features.name: Data freshness
features.does: Every market view shows which release it uses and when it was loaded, so you can judge the figures before using them.

areas.name: Public data library
areas.intro: More than 150 public healthcare datasets from CMS, NPPES, the U.S. Census Bureau, HRSA, CDC, AHRQ, BLS, the HHS Office of Inspector General and state licensing agencies, linked by NPI, CCN, county and ZIP.

features.name: Providers and clinicians
features.does: Every individual and organization in the national NPI registry, with practice locations, NUCC specialties and affiliations, kept current from CMS’s weekly files. Add Medicare services and payments by clinician, home health certifications, hospice care-plan oversight, Order & Referring enrollment, Part D prescribing and MIPS scores.

features.name: Facilities, quality and ownership
features.does: Provider of Services and Care Compare files for hospitals, home health agencies, hospices, nursing homes, inpatient rehab and long-term care hospitals: star ratings, patient surveys, readmissions, inspections, penalties, nurse staffing, ownership and chains, plus cost reports for hospitals, home health agencies, hospices and nursing homes.

features.name: Medicare use and market activity
features.does: Home health, hospice and skilled nursing use and supply by county, post-acute utilization by provider, spending and readmissions by county, Hospital Service Areas, inpatient diagnosis groups and outpatient services, DME by supplier and referring provider, and monthly Medicare enrollment.

features.name: Demographics and growth
features.does: American Community Survey 5-year estimates for every county and ZIP area (ages 65+, 75+ and 85+, median age, income, home value, poverty, uninsured, disability, living alone and dual coverage) and Census population estimates of the change since April 2020.

features.name: Payers and Medicare Advantage
features.does: Medicare Advantage enrollment by organization, contract and county, penetration, plan star ratings and supplemental benefits; Medicaid managed care plans where CMS publishes them; and marketplace insurers by county.

features.name: Community health and need
features.does: CDC PLACES disease and disability prevalence, the CDC Social Vulnerability Index, AHRQ social determinants of health, HRSA shortage and medically underserved areas, the HRSA Area Health Resources File, Mapping Medicare Disparities, BLS healthcare wages, County Business Patterns and VA facilities.

features.name: Provider standing and payments
features.does: A provider’s page flags an OIG exclusion, a Medicare opt-out or revocation and the next revalidation date, and shows Open Payments totals from drug and device makers, so you can check standing before you invest in a relationship.

features.name: State-licensed homes
features.does: Personal care, assisted living, memory care and domiciliary care homes and their beds, imported from each state’s licensing file and counted in county and ZIP area figures. In a state whose file is loaded, an area with none reads 0.

features.name: Releases checked daily
features.does: The CMS catalogs are checked every day for new releases, and stored rows are refreshed when one arrives. Data years more than ten years old are removed, and a dataset its publisher stopped releasing is retired instead of shown as current.

areas.name: Competitor intelligence
areas.intro: Who you compete with for referrals, how they are moving, and what to say about it.

features.name: Competitor rankings
features.does: Home health agencies and hospices in your territory ranked by Medicare share, with each one’s star rating and change. Download the rankings as CSV.

features.name: Watchlist and alerts
features.does: Follow the competitors that matter and get alerts when a star rating, owner or service area changes, a change of ownership is filed, or a new provider opens nearby.

features.name: Compare and trends
features.does: Put competitors side by side on market rank, Medicare patients, share and its change, star rating, locations and ZIP codes served, and follow their share over time.

features.name: County roll-up
features.does: Every county in a state with its market leader, number of agencies and biggest mover, as CSV or a leadership-brief PDF.

features.name: Scheduled leadership brief
features.does: Email the county roll-up as a PDF to your managers daily, weekly or monthly.

features.name: What to say
features.does: On a home health agency or hospice, a card lines your organization up with the three largest in the county on star rating, patient survey and Medicare patient totals, in plain sentences.

features.name: Free agency market review
features.does: On the public site, anyone can type a home health or hospice CCN and get a PDF by email: the agency's Medicare patients, share and rank in its county and state, the largest local agencies and its public CMS ratings.

areas.name: Manager and team tools
areas.intro: Set expectations, see where the effort goes, and coach the people doing the work.

features.name: Goals and leaderboard
features.does: Monthly visit and referral targets for each marketer, a leaderboard, Met / On pace / Behind for the open month and a six-month trend. Everyone sees their own progress on Today.

features.name: Team review
features.does: One marketer’s week in one place: visits and calls with their notes, saved routes, open tasks and assigned accounts.

features.name: Activity report and weekly email
features.does: Visits, calls, tasks done and overdue, referrals and admissions by person and source, new and lost sources, stage changes and accounts not visited. Download a spreadsheet or PDF, or turn on a weekly email.

features.name: Coaching
features.does: Ride-along notes, comments on a visit and 1-on-1s for one marketer.

features.name: Locations
features.does: Add locations and assign each person as a marketer or manager. People then see their locations’ accounts, and reports follow the same rule.

features.name: Book balance
features.does: Proposes a split of accounts across the marketers you choose by referral potential and drive time. Nothing moves until a manager applies it.

features.name: Account briefs and Ask the book
features.does: A short factual brief on any account (stage, visits, calls and referral outcomes over 90 days, with notes left out), and answers to supported questions about your book, such as the top ten sources last quarter.

features.name: Decision briefs
features.does: Prioritized accounts to prepare for, manager exceptions such as overdue tasks and falling referrals, and changes on the accounts you watch. Download a branded PDF or CSV, or have it emailed.

features.name: Materials library
features.does: Brochures, physician one-pagers, service-line flyers and video links in one searchable place. New versions replace old ones, marketers note what they left on a visit, and managers see who opened each file.

features.name: Healthcare observances
features.does: A calendar of the days, weeks and months that honor the people marketers call on (Doctors’ Day, Nurse Practitioner Week, Case Management Week, Social Work Month, Nurses Week and more), care settings, health awareness months and Medicare enrollment periods, worked out each year from the sponsor’s rule. Today and the Monday digest show what is coming up; Remind me adds a task two weeks ahead, and the calendar downloads for Outlook, Google Calendar or a phone.

features.name: AI Assistant
features.does: Ask about your market, your book and your day in plain English. It looks answers up in the app’s data inside your plan’s territory, says when a figure is an estimate, and proposes lead lists, visits, tasks, call plans and outreach drafts that are saved only when you confirm. Each question uses one of your organization’s daily AI requests.
features.access: Growth & Pro · organization admins, and the team when turned on

features.name: AI playbook
features.does: An organization admin sets the pitch pillars, the service lines to mention and the words to avoid. The pre-visit card adds a pillar when it has room, and the notes summary and spoken debrief follow the playbook and flag an avoided word.

features.name: Use your own AI app with Intel
features.does: Make a personal token in Account and connect an AI app that supports MCP to Intel. It reads providers, lead scores, county and market facts, your day, account briefs, lead lists and your book as you, with your role and your plan’s places, and can’t change anything. Each question counts toward your organization’s AI requests.
features.access: Growth & Pro · whoever can open the AI Assistant

features.name: Activity challenges and report card
features.does: Set a friendly target for visits, calls, accounts touched or tier A visits for a location or the whole organization, with standings for everyone in it. Never referrals or admissions, with a reminder about contractors paid on a 1099. Each person's report card compares their month's activity with the month before.

areas.name: Email campaigns
areas.intro: Reach the contacts on a lead list or your book, with sending rules that protect your reputation.

features.name: Campaigns to lists and contacts
features.does: Email a lead list, the contacts on one line of your book, or both. People marked as left are skipped.

features.name: Delivery tracking
features.does: Track deliveries, opens, clicks and bounces for each campaign, and link campaigns to the accounts they touched.

features.name: Sender and unsubscribe
features.does: Set the name recipients see, where replies go and your postal address. Every email carries an unsubscribe link that is honored automatically.

features.name: Queue contacts from an account
features.does: Any marketer can add a contact to a draft campaign from the account page; an owner prepares and sends it.

features.name: Nurture sequences
features.does: Start a sequence of calls, visits, emails and tasks on an account, from four starters (new physician welcome, in-service thank-you, quarterly outcomes packet, re-engage a slipping source) or your own. Email steps carry a draft you send from Follow-up. A sequence stops on its own on a referral, a contact leaving or every contact unsubscribing, or when you mark a reply.

areas.name: Reports and analytics
areas.intro: Your book turned into reports that managers, owners and marketers can each trust for their own scope.

features.name: Results reports
features.does: Performance scorecard, field activity, tasks and follow-up, mileage, referrals and admissions, top referral sources, why referrals were not admitted, payer mix, source pipeline, account coverage and goal attainment.

features.name: Source quality after admission
features.does: Load a stays report (or have a supported EMR deliver it on a schedule) and see, by referral source, marketer or location, how long patients stay, short stays, hospice live discharges and revocations, and home health returns to the hospital, plus average daily census against each location's budget. A group is rated only with 10 or more endings, a flag means 10 points above your own average, and patient columns are never read or stored.
features.access: Loading and organization budgets: owners · by marketer and location: managers

features.name: Filter and group
features.does: Choose dates, then filter and group by person, location, line of business, account type, county, payer, source type, month or week. Members see their own work; managers see their locations; owners see the company.

features.name: PDF, Excel and CSV
features.does: Every report downloads with the same figures as the screen and the source of the data printed on it.

features.name: Custom report builder
features.does: Save charts and email them on a schedule to up to 25 people in your organization.

areas.name: Administration, security and data
areas.intro: Control who can see what, keep a record of it, and know where every figure comes from.

features.name: Organization, people and roles
features.does: Invite people up to your plan’s seats, make someone an owner or a member, disable accounts, send password reset links and sign someone out everywhere.

features.name: Text-message sign-in codes
features.does: Owners and location managers can add a six-digit code, sent by text, to their own sign-in.

features.name: Security audit
features.does: Sign-ins, account changes, exports and other recorded actions for your organization, with filters.

features.name: Billing and territory
features.does: Choose your plan, counties or states and add-ons (extra seats, locations and states) from Billing.

features.name: Guided setup and help
features.does: A guided setup for a new organization, an in-app help guide, and illustrated user guides for marketers and administrators as PDFs.

features.name: Business menu and search
features.does: Pick a healthcare service line to focus your CRM, referral tracking, and available research views. Use Other healthcare services for an unlisted specialty. Public datasets and specialized reports vary by setting. Press Ctrl+K anywhere to search accounts, providers, NPIs, lead lists and pages.

features.name: Public data, clearly sourced
features.does: Provider, facility and market figures come from CMS, NPPES, the U.S. Census Bureau and state licensing files, with each dataset’s release shown. Public research uses no patient-level data.

features.name: Patient privacy by design
features.does: Patient-identifying columns are dropped from referral imports, briefs and scorecards leave notes out, and exports carry no patient names.

features.name: Send data out
features.does: An organization admin sends the organization’s own accounts, referrals and visit counts out every night: three CSV files to an SFTP server whose host key you pin, or accounts to a supported CRM as companies. Notes, check-in positions and patient details never leave Intel; passwords and tokens are stored encrypted.

data.headline: Every provider in your market, with their Medicare activity.
includes: Every individual and organization in the national NPI registry, with practice locations, specialties and affiliations, refreshed from CMS’s weekly files
Medicare services, patients and payments by clinician, home health certifications and hospice care-plan oversight by physician
Order & Referring enrollment, Part D prescribing, MIPS quality scores and Open Payments totals
OIG exclusions, Medicare opt-outs and revocations, flagged on the provider’s page
data.source: NPPES, the NUCC taxonomy, CMS Physician & Other Practitioners, Order & Referring, Part D Prescribers, the Quality Payment Program, Open Payments and the OIG exclusion list
data.question: Which physicians and practices should we call on first?
data.decision: Compare clinicians by specialty, location, and available Medicare activity, see who opened or moved a practice, and review public standing before investing in a relationship.
data.limit: A provider’s presence or activity is a research signal, not a promise of referrals. CMS lists a clinician’s counts only above ten patients.

data.headline: Every Medicare facility, with quality, ownership and finances.
includes: Hospitals, home health agencies, hospices, nursing homes, inpatient rehab, long-term care hospitals, DME suppliers and community health centers
Star ratings, patient surveys, readmissions, inspections, penalties and nurse staffing
Ownership, chains, changes of ownership and cost-report revenue, expenses, beds and visits
The Hospice Care Index, home health value-based purchasing scores and CMS TEAM hospitals
State-licensed personal care, assisted living and memory care homes and beds, where loaded
data.source: CMS Provider of Services, Care Compare, cost reports (HCRIS), ownership and staffing files, and available state licensing files
data.question: Which facilities should we partner with, and who are we up against?
data.decision: Walk into a hospital or nursing home already knowing its ratings, ownership, size and service area, and print a branded profile for the visit.
data.limit: Licensed-home coverage and available detail vary by state and source. Measures describe the periods CMS publishes.

data.headline: See where Medicare patients go, county by county.
includes: Home health, hospice and skilled nursing use and supply by county
Medicare spending per beneficiary and readmissions by county
Where each county’s residents are hospitalized and where post-discharge spending goes
Each agency’s share of the Medicare patients served, from Care Compare ZIP service areas
Inpatient diagnosis groups, outpatient services, and DME by supplier and referring provider
data.source: CMS Market Saturation, Geographic Variation, Hospital Service Area, Post-Acute Care utilization, inpatient, outpatient and DME files
data.question: Where is the volume, and who is capturing it?
data.decision: Review the Medicare volume available for your service line alongside local provider supply and hospital activity before assigning outreach resources.
data.limit: Post-discharge spending is a planning indicator, not a count of transfers. Medicare populations and coverage vary by dataset and service line.

data.headline: Know the people in every county and ZIP area.
includes: Residents 65+, 75+ and 85+, median age, household income and home value for every county and ZIP area
Poverty, uninsured, disability, Medicare-Medicaid dual coverage and older adults living alone
Population change since the 2020 Census, for all ages and for 65+, 75+ and 85+
A Site finder that ranks counties or ZIP areas by demand, growth, need and supply gap for your service line
data.source: U.S. Census Bureau 2020 geography, American Community Survey 5-year estimates and population estimates
data.question: Where should we open, expand or send more marketing time?
data.decision: Compare local demand with the providers already there before you hire, open an office or redraw territories.
data.limit: Demographic estimates provide planning context; they do not identify individual prospects. A ZIP area carries its county’s growth.

data.headline: Understand the payer mix behind your market.
includes: Medicare enrollment and Medicare Advantage share by county
Medicare Advantage enrollment by organization and plan, plan star ratings and supplemental benefits
Medicaid managed care plans where CMS publishes them, and marketplace insurers by county
data.source: CMS Medicare Monthly Enrollment, Medicare Advantage enrollment, star rating and plan benefit files, and marketplace public use files
data.question: Which plans do our patients carry, and how is the mix changing?
data.decision: Plan payer conversations and outreach with the county’s current Medicare Advantage penetration and the plans that hold the most members.
data.limit: Enrollment is by county of residence, for the period CMS published.

data.headline: See health need and access in every county.
includes: Chronic disease and disability prevalence and Social Vulnerability Index ranks
Health professional shortage areas and medically underserved areas
Social determinants of health, Mapping Medicare Disparities rates and Older Americans Act services by state
Healthcare wages and employers, VA facilities and the home health wage index
data.source: CDC PLACES and Social Vulnerability Index, HRSA, AHRQ, the CMS Office of Minority Health, ACL, BLS, Census County Business Patterns and the VA
data.question: Where is need highest and access weakest?
data.decision: Find the communities that most need your services, and see local wage levels for the staff you would hire before you expand.
data.limit: Measures are county-level estimates from each publisher’s latest release.

data.headline: Track every competing agency and hospice.
includes: Home health agencies and hospices ranked by Medicare share, with star ratings and change from the prior period
Alerts when a competitor’s star rating, owner or service area changes, or a new provider opens nearby
Side-by-side comparisons, share trends and a county roll-up of each market leader and biggest mover
A plain-language card comparing your agency with the three largest in the county
data.source: CMS Care Compare, ZIP service areas, Provider of Services and ownership files
data.question: Who are we losing to, and what should we say about it?
data.decision: Spot a rival’s weakness or a new entrant early, and give marketers facts to use in the next conversation.
data.limit: Rankings describe the periods CMS publishes, not this week’s referrals.

data.headline: Keep your organization’s work and results together.
includes: Accounts, contacts, ownership, calls, visits, and follow-ups
Expenses, receipts, approvals, reimbursements, and mileage
Recorded or CSV-imported referrals and admissions, with response times
Source trends, conversion, lost reasons, team activity, and goals
data.source: The information your organization records or imports
data.question: Where should we follow up, coach the team, or change the plan?
data.decision: Reduce the time spent reconstructing account history and bring recorded results into the conversation about marketing priorities.
data.limit: Results reflect your records. CSV imports are file-based, not live EMR connections; patient-identifying columns are dropped.

faq.question: Who is CareMetric Intel for?
faq.answer: CareMetric Intel is built for home health agencies, hospice agencies, hospitals, nursing homes, and personal care homes that want to grow their share of referrals. Physician practices and clinics, behavioral health, rehabilitation and therapy, diagnostics, dialysis, DME, and other healthcare organizations can use it too. Owners, managers, marketers, and liaisons can research referral sources, coordinate outreach, manage relationships, and track recorded results. Choose your service lines within your plan’s allowance; specialized public-data coverage varies by setting.

faq.question: Is CareMetric Intel a CRM?
faq.answer: Yes. Alongside market, territory, and competitor research, CareMetric Intel is a CRM built for healthcare and senior-care marketers. It keeps a marketing book of accounts with stages, contacts by healthcare role, visits, calls, notes, tasks and follow-ups, referrals and admissions, expenses and mileage, and the reports managers use to review the team. The All features page lists every feature and the plan that includes it.

faq.question: What data does CareMetric Intel include?
faq.answer: More than 150 public healthcare datasets, linked by NPI, CCN, county and ZIP. Providers: every individual and organization in the national NPI registry, with Medicare services by clinician, home health certifications, hospice care-plan oversight, Order & Referring enrollment, Part D prescribing, MIPS scores, Open Payments totals and OIG exclusions. Facilities: hospitals, home health agencies, hospices, nursing homes, inpatient rehab, long-term care hospitals, DME suppliers and community health centers, with star ratings, patient surveys, inspections, staffing, ownership and cost reports, plus state-licensed personal care and assisted living homes where loaded. Markets: Medicare use, supply, spending, readmissions and market share by county. People: Census demographics and growth for every county and ZIP area. Payers: Medicare Advantage enrollment, penetration, star ratings and benefits. Community: CDC, HRSA, AHRQ and BLS measures of health, need and workforce. Coverage varies by dataset and geography, and the Data sources & use page lists every source.

faq.question: How is this different from a general-purpose CRM?
faq.answer: A general-purpose CRM starts empty and knows nothing about healthcare. CareMetric Intel comes with the public market data already linked to your accounts, so a hospital or practice on your book shows its Medicare volume, star ratings, market share and rank beside your own history. It also has what healthcare marketing needs out of the box: contacts by role from discharge planner to director of nursing, referral and admission tracking with lost reasons, EMR report imports, the Stark annual limit on marketing spend, outcomes packets for hospitals and competitor alerts. Onboarding is free on every plan.

faq.question: How does this help save time and money?
faq.answer: CareMetric Intel helps your team research accounts, focus its target lists, prepare calls and visits, and keep follow-ups and referral records together. That gives managers a practical way to reduce repeated research, unfocused outreach, and missed next steps. The time and cost benefit depends on your team’s use of the tools; no specific savings or referral increase is guaranteed.

faq.question: How does referral tracking work?
faq.answer: Your team can record referrals and admissions against accounts or import supported referral facts from CSV reports. Review source trends, conversion, and lost reasons alongside the outreach your team logs. Public market patterns and opportunity scores remain research signals and are not treated as confirmed referrals.

faq.question: Can marketers track expenses and mileage?
faq.answer: Yes. Marketers log each expense against the account it was for, start from a receipt photo, and list who attended so a shared meal is valued per person. Each physician’s running total is tracked against the Stark nonmonetary-compensation limit, and per-meal caps, meal frequency, missing receipts, and possible duplicates are flagged. Managers approve or deny, record reimbursement, and export register, compliance, and payroll reports. Mileage adds the straight-line distance between a day’s visit check-ins at your organization’s rate. These tools support your compliance program; they are not legal advice.

faq.question: What can we explore during the free trial?
faq.answer: The 30-day trial covers one county and includes three marketer seats and one manager seat. Create your organization account, select the county in Billing, and explore the available research, planning, and reporting tools. A labeled sample book gives you examples to work through. A credit card is required before trial access opens. Your selected plan bills automatically after the trial unless you cancel first.

faq.question: Can we keep an eye on competitors?
faq.answer: Yes. Research providers and facilities across specialties using their locations, ownership, and available public measures. The Competitors share rankings, watchlists, and change alerts use home health and hospice Medicare datasets. Those specialized analyses describe the populations and periods in those sources; other settings can use provider and facility research alongside their own referral records.

faq.question: Does public-data analysis show confirmed referrals?
faq.answer: Public provider activity and opportunity scores provide research context. They do not establish a confirmed referral relationship. Your organization’s referral and admission reporting uses the facts your team records or imports into its marketing book.

faq.question: How current is the market information?
faq.answer: Each source has its own reporting period and publishing schedule. CareMetric Intel checks the CMS catalogs every day for new releases, refreshes the stored data when one arrives, and shows each dataset’s release and load date in the app so you can assess the information before using it. Data years more than ten years old are removed, and a dataset whose publisher stopped releasing it is retired rather than shown as current. Coverage and available detail vary by dataset, geography, and care setting.

faq.question: Can we import results from our EMR reports?
faq.answer: Owners can import referral and admission facts from CSV files, map their columns, and review a preview before saving. Use column mapping for your organization’s report, or start from a saved layout for a common home health or hospice EMR report. These are file-based imports, not live EMR connections.

faq.question: Can we use the platform across locations?
faq.answer: Yes. Growth includes up to three locations, and Pro includes up to ten. Assign people to locations, organize account ownership, and review reports within their access scope. Plan limits and purchased add-ons determine the territory and team size your organization can use.

faq.question: Does CareMetric Intel use patient-level data?
faq.answer: The public research tools use provider, facility, and aggregated market information. Patient-identifying columns are dropped during referral-file imports. Keep patient names, diagnoses, and other patient information out of free-text notes and support requests. The Data sources & use page explains the information and its permitted use.

faq.question: What do the AI features help with?
faq.answer: Where receipt reading is configured, a receipt photo is read into an expense draft for you to check. Ask the book answers supported questions about your marketing book with fixed reports, such as your top sources last quarter. Availability depends on your plan, your role, and the services configured for your organization. Review generated text and figures before using them in outreach or business decisions.

caveats: Feature availability and usage limits vary by plan. Opportunity scores support research and outreach planning. AI-assisted features depend on supported reports and configured services. Expense compliance tools support your compliance program; they are not legal advice.

Coverage depends on the dataset, geography, reporting period, and your plan. Not every field is available in every market. Medicare measures describe the populations and periods included in the source; public patterns do not confirm individual referrals.

Patient-identifying columns are dropped from referral imports, and notes should never name a patient.
